## Purpose

This SOP describes the deployment, data retrieval, and barometric
compensation of Onset HOBO water level loggers for continuous
monitoring of water surface elevation in streams, lakes, wetlands,
and groundwater wells. Continuous stage records are essential for
developing stage-discharge rating curves, characterizing hydrologic
response to storms, and documenting seasonal water table fluctuations.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Onset HOBO U20, U20L, and MX2001 water level loggers
  deployed at EA Program surface water and groundwater monitoring sites
- **Does not apply to:** Real-time telemetered stage recorders;
  acoustic or radar level sensors; staff gauge readings (visual
  observations recorded in the field notebook)
- **Location:** All EA Program hydrologic monitoring sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Approve deployment locations and logging intervals      |
| Trained Personnel | Deploy, retrieve, and download loggers per this SOP     |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use                |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Deployment sites may involve steep banks, slippery
  surfaces, swift water, or confined spaces (well casings). Work in
  pairs at all stream and well sites.
- **Drowning:** Do not deploy loggers during high-flow events. Never
  wade in flows deeper than waist height.
- **Biological:** Waterborne pathogens; ticks and snakes in riparian
  areas.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Wading boots or chest waders (stream deployments)
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes (well deployments)
- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd). A minimum
of two people must be present for all in-stream deployments.


## Instrument Specifications

### HOBO U20L Water Level Logger

| Parameter              | Value                                      |
|:-----------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Measurement principle  | Absolute pressure (water + atmosphere)     |
| Pressure range         | 0--9 m (30 ft) or 0--4 m (13 ft) depth models |
| Accuracy               | +/- 0.1% full scale (typical 0.5 cm water) |
| Resolution             | 0.02% full scale                           |
| Temperature range      | -20 to 50 C                                |
| Temperature accuracy   | +/- 0.44 C from 0 to 40 C                 |
| Logging interval       | 1 second to 18 hours (user-configurable)   |
| Memory                 | 64 KB (approximately 21,700 combined pressure and temperature readings) |
| Battery                | 3V lithium; approximately 5-year life at 1-minute logging |
| Communication          | Optical USB coupler (U20L) or Bluetooth (MX2001) |

### HOBO MX2001 Water Level Logger

| Parameter              | Value                                      |
|:-----------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Communication          | Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE); download via HOBOconnect app |
| Pressure range         | 0--9 m (30 ft) or 0--4 m (13 ft) models   |
| Other specifications   | Similar to U20L                            |

### Barometric Reference Logger

Because the water level loggers measure absolute pressure (water column
plus atmosphere), a companion barometric pressure logger must be
deployed above the water surface at or near the site. Onset HOBO U20L-04
(barometric model) or a HOBO MX barometric logger serves this purpose.


## Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| HOBO U20L or MX2001 water level logger | Confirm depth range matches site        |
| HOBO barometric reference logger       | One per site or cluster of nearby sites |
| Optical USB coupler (BASE-U-4) for U20L | For launching and downloading          |
| HOBOware Pro software (laptop)         | For U20L launch, download, and compensation |
| HOBOconnect app (smartphone)           | For MX2001 launch and download          |
| Stilling well or PVC housing           | Perforated PVC pipe (2--4 inch diameter); protects logger from debris |
| Cable tie or stainless steel wire      | For securing logger inside stilling well |
| Rebar stake or concrete anchor         | For anchoring the stilling well to the streambed |
| Staff gauge or graduated tape          | For reference stage readings            |
| Measuring tape and level               | For surveying the logger elevation      |
| Field notebook                         | For recording deployment metadata       |
| GPS unit                               | For recording deployment coordinates    |


## Procedure

### Pre-Deployment Setup

1. **Launch the logger** using HOBOware (U20L) or HOBOconnect (MX2001):
   - Set the logging interval: 15 minutes is standard for most
     hydrologic monitoring; use 5 minutes for flashy urban streams or
     1 minute for storm event capture.
   - Set a delayed start time so all loggers at a site begin recording
     simultaneously.
   - Verify the logger clock is synchronized to the correct time zone
     (Pacific Time).
2. **Launch the barometric reference logger** with the same logging
   interval and start time.
3. Record in the field notebook: logger serial number, model, logging
   interval, start time, and battery status.

### Stream Deployment

1. Select a deployment location in a pool or low-velocity area where
   the logger will remain submerged during low-flow conditions.
   Avoid locations subject to scour, heavy debris, or vandalism.
2. Install the stilling well:
   - Drive a rebar stake into the streambed in a stable location.
   - Attach the perforated PVC housing to the stake with cable ties
     or hose clamps. The housing should be vertical with the bottom
     anchored and the top above the expected high-water level.
   - Ensure the perforations face upstream and downstream to allow
     free water exchange.
3. Lower the logger into the stilling well and secure it with a
   stainless steel wire or cable tie. The logger should hang freely
   and not rest on the bottom.
4. Record the deployment elevation:
   - Measure the distance from the top of the stilling well to the
     water surface and to the logger sensor.
   - If a staff gauge is installed, read and record the current stage.
   - Record GPS coordinates per
     [SOP-F006](SOP-F006-gps-site-navigation.qmd).
5. Deploy the barometric reference logger nearby, above the high-water
   line, in a shaded and ventilated location (e.g., inside a
   radiation shield attached to a tree or post). Do not seal it in
   an airtight container.
6. Take a photograph of the deployment.

### Well Deployment

1. Remove the well cap and measure the depth to water using an
   electronic water level indicator (e-tape). Record the measurement.
2. Lower the logger into the well on a stainless steel cable or
   braided fishing line. Position the logger below the lowest expected
   water level but above the well screen bottom.
3. Secure the suspension cable to the well cap or casing.
4. Record the logger depth below the top of casing (TOC) and the
   TOC elevation if surveyed.
5. Replace the well cap.
6. Deploy the barometric reference logger at the wellhead or at a
   nearby location above ground.

### Data Retrieval

Retrieve data at intervals appropriate for the project (typically
monthly or quarterly). The logger continues recording during download.

**U20L (optical coupler):**

1. Remove the logger from the stilling well or well.
2. Attach the optical USB coupler and connect to the laptop.
3. In HOBOware, select **Readout** to download data. The logger
   continues recording after readout.
4. Return the logger to its deployment position.

**MX2001 (Bluetooth):**

1. Open the HOBOconnect app on a smartphone within Bluetooth range
   (approximately 30 m line of sight).
2. Select the logger and tap **Readout**.
3. The logger does not need to be removed from the water for download.

### Barometric Compensation

Raw data from the water level logger must be compensated for
atmospheric pressure changes before the readings represent true water
level.

1. In HOBOware, open the water level logger file and the barometric
   reference logger file.
2. Select **Data Assistant > Barometric Compensation**.
3. Specify the reference water level: enter a staff gauge reading or
   a known water surface elevation at a specific date and time.
4. HOBOware subtracts the barometric pressure from the absolute
   pressure to yield the water column height and converts to the
   reference datum.
5. Export the compensated data as `.csv`.
6. Save using the naming convention:
   `YYYY-MM-DD_SiteID_waterlevel_compensated.csv`
7. Upload to the project GitHub repository under `data/stage/`.

### Logger Retrieval (End of Deployment)

1. Download all remaining data.
2. Remove the logger and stilling well hardware.
3. Rinse the logger with clean water and dry.
4. Remove any biofouling (algae, mineral deposits) from the pressure
   port using a soft brush. Do not insert anything into the port.
5. Store the logger in a dry location.


## Quality Control

- At every site visit, read the staff gauge (or measure depth to water
  in wells) and record the time. Use these manual readings to verify
  the logger data during post-processing.
- Compare the barometric logger against a nearby weather station
  (NWS or CIMIS) to confirm the reference pressure is reasonable.
- If two loggers are deployed at the same site, compare their records.
  Readings should agree within 1 cm.
- Inspect loggers for biofouling and sediment accumulation at every
  download visit. Heavy fouling can dampen pressure response.
- Flag and investigate any sudden offsets or drift in the compensated
  water level record (may indicate logger movement, sedimentation, or
  battery failure).

## Training Record

Before deploying water level loggers independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Demonstrate logger programming (launch, interval, delayed start)
   using HOBOware or HOBOconnect
3. Participate in a supervised stream or well deployment
4. Demonstrate barometric compensation in HOBOware and export of
   compensated data
5. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
